mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has improved steadily from -9.7 to -8.4 over the last four weeks, indicating a gradual return of office-based commuting. This restored commuting pattern feeds adjacent retail and recreation footfall, so RETAIL_REC should continue to rise over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES rose from -9.7 to -8.4 over four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 28-day forward mean is lower than its 28-day trailing mean despite WORKPLACES continuing its upward trend, the hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: TRANSIT mobility has recovered sharply from -31.0 to -27.3 in the latest week. Once TRANSIT crosses above -28, commuters and shoppers resume public-transit-dependent retail trips, pushing RETAIL_REC higher within two weeks of the crossing.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -28 for at least one week after being below -28 the prior week
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks of TRANSIT crossing above -28, or falls further, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous improvement in WORKPLACES (-9.7 to -8.4) and TRANSIT (-31.0 to -27.3) jointly signal a compounding resumption of daily commuting and errand-running that amplifies retail footfall beyond what either series would predict alone, producing a stronger rise in RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:both WORKPLACES and TRANSIT improved concurrently over the last four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC rise is no larger than that predicted by either WORKPLACES or TRANSIT alone (no synergistic uplift), or if RETAIL_REC fails to rise despite both series improving, the interaction hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RESIDENTIAL mobility has declined steadily from 6.6 to 3.7 over four weeks, indicating easing stay-at-home behavior consistent with relaxed restrictions. In an easing-restrictions regime, this declining residential trend translates into more out-of-home retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL fell from 6.6 to 3.7 over four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise while RESIDENTIAL continues to fall, or if the regime shifts to renewed restrictions and RESIDENTIAL rises instead, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility shows volatile seasonal decline, dropping sharply to -27.3 at t-1w before partially recovering to -16.9, consistent with approaching cooler/festive season shifting outdoor leisure indoors. This seasonal substitution redirects recreational activity toward retail venues, lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell to -27.3 at t-1w then rebounded to -16.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC does not rise within two weeks despite PARKS remaining depressed relative to its four-week average, the seasonal substitution hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM mobility has been slowly declining from 2.3 to 1.3 over four weeks, suggesting households are normalizing essential-trip frequency rather than stockpiling. This signals waning precautionary behavior, allowing discretionary RETAIL_REC trips to rise modestly within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM declined from 2.3 to 1.3 over four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's next-week mean does not rise relative to the current week despite continued GROCERY_PHARM decline, the hypothesis fails.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp one-week PARKS drop from -17.1 to -27.3 followed by a rebound to -16.9 indicates an erratic, possibly weather- or event-driven mobility shock. Such volatility signals short-term consumer uncertainty that suppresses planned retail outings, so if PARKS volatility (week-over-week swing) exceeds 8 points, RETAIL_REC growth stalls or reverses within one week.
candidate_trigger: absolute week-over-week change in PARKS exceeds 8 points
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS swung from -17.1 to -27.3 to -16.9 across consecutive weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC continues to rise in the week following a PARKS swing greater than 8 points, the volatility-suppression hypothesis is rejected.

mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC itself has shown a consistent improving trend from -8.0 to -7.0 over the last four weeks, reflecting positive momentum in consumer footfall. This autoregressive momentum is expected to persist, driving RETAIL_REC modestly higher over the next four weeks absent any shock.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -8.0 to -7.0 over four weeks
failure_condition: If RETAIL_REC's 28-day forward mean is equal to or lower than its 28-day trailing mean despite the observed four-week improving trend, the momentum hypothesis is rejected.
